card.name: Words just before a clinical detail
card.fires_on: Short connecting or lead-in words in drug-label text, such as 'included', 'no', 'with', 'to' or 'dose', right before a list of symptoms, effects or standards. It is most common in overdosage and toxicity passages.

modes.label: Overdosage lead-ins
modes.description: Words such as 'included', 'no' or 'dose' in overdose sections just before symptoms or experience are named.
modes.example: 10 OVERDOSAGE There has been<< no>> experience of overdosage in human clinical

modes.label: Linking words before toxicity or care terms
modes.description: Words such as 'with', 'to' or 'mechanism' that lead into a toxicity term or a standard of care.
modes.example: accumulate aluminum at levels associated<< with>> central nervous system and bone toxicity.

modes.label: Table row labels
modes.description: A starting word in a dosing table row, such as an age group.
modes.example: Age Group Starting Dose<< Birth>> (gestational age at least 3
